title: loading on button
rule: For a slow action, show loading on the button itself (spinner on the control that was pressed).

citation.source: NN/g — Button States: Communicate Interaction; Apple HIG — Buttons (activity indicator when the action does not complete instantly)

pass_when: A slow action shows a spinner/activity indicator on the pressed button itself.
fail_when: No loading on a slow action, or loading only elsewhere (page bar, toast) with none on the control.
overview: Slow actions show a spinner on the pressed button itself.
apply_when: An action takes noticeable time after the person presses the control.
not_when: Instant actions that complete before loading feedback would register.
agent_hint: Put the loading spinner on the pressed button, not only elsewhere.
description: When an action is slow, feedback belongs on the control that was pressed so the person sees that press was accepted. Show a spinner or activity indicator on that button itself; a page-level progress bar or toast alone leaves the pressed control looking idle and uncertain. Skip loading chrome for actions that finish immediately—there is nothing to wait for. Use on-button loading whenever completion is not instant and the person needs confirmation that the same control is working.
